details.description: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct is Meta's smallest instruction-tuned model in the Llama 3.1 family, released July 23, 2024 and trained on about 15 trillion tokens of publicly available data. It's an 8-billion-parameter auto-regressive transformer with a 128K-token context window, built for multilingual assistant-style chat, tool calling, and lightweight fine-tuning or edge deployment, with a knowledge cutoff of December 2023. Amazon Bedrock's current model card lists this model's lifecycle status as Active.
advantages: Scores 84.5% on GSM8K (grade-school math with chain-of-thought), per Meta's model card.
Scores 72.6% on HumanEval for code generation, per Meta's model card.
Supports tool/function calling, scoring 76.1% on the Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) and 82.6% on API-Bank, per Meta's model card.
128K-token context window despite its compact 8-billion-parameter size, making it suitable for fine-tuning and edge deployment.
disadvantages: Text-only; no image, audio, or video input or output.
Officially supports only 8 languages (English, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish, Thai) despite training on a broader language collection, per Meta's model card.
use_cases: Fine-tuning for specialized or on-device/edge deployments.

notes: Catalog's max_output_tokens is 2048; Amazon Bedrock's own model card for this exact Bedrock model ID (meta.llama3-1-8b-instruct-v1:0 / us.meta.llama3-1-8b-instruct-v1:0) lists a 4K max output token limit instead, but the catalog value was kept per instructions. AWS Bedrock lists this model's lifecycle status as Active, consistent with the catalog's empty deprecation_date. Meta's own llama.com/developer.meta.com model-card pages redirected to a login screen and could not be read directly, so this write-up relies on Meta's GitHub and Hugging Face model cards plus AWS Bedrock's status page.
